packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-04: UNVERIFIED IMAGE-ONLY READING

EXPOSURE AND METHOD STATEMENT
- My context did not contain any proposed identification of this text or any earlier transcription of it. I opened only PROMPT.md and image-001 to image-042 of packet-04. I did not open packet.json and used no web or search tool.
- Disclosure: while reading, I recognised from general familiarity that several red-underlined lemmata read like Latin Psalter verses. I did not consult any edition and did not use memory to fill gaps. Everything below transcribes letters I can see. Where a word is only partly visible I give the visible letters and mark the rest [illegible] or with "?".
- A modern pencil note in the lower margin reads "Stams, STA, Frg. 213r" (image-001/020) and "Stams, STA, Frg. 213v" (image-022/042). Below I call the two faces "r" and "v" to match those notes.

CONVENTIONS
- "img-NNN Lk" means image-NNN.jpg, line k counted from the top of that image. I count only text lines of the column being transcribed. A line cut by the image edge counts as a line.
- (..) marks an expansion I propose. "?" after a reading means it is uncertain. [illegible] marks unreadable text. [hole] marks loss of the support. LEMMA marks text underlined in red.
- Tiles overlap. When a line appears in two tiles I give it once and cite both tiles.

=====================================================================
FACE r (overview image-001; tiles image-002 to image-021, 5 across x 4 down)
=====================================================================
LAYOUT SURVEY (observation)
- An opened bifolium, upright, with two pages, each written in two columns. The vertical bounding lines are ruled in red.
- Script: a small, upright late-Romanesque / early-Gothic book hand with heavy abbreviation. Some passages are underlined in red. These look like quoted text (lemmata) followed by explanatory prose; that reading of their function is an interpretation. Some underlined lemmata begin with a brown or red enlarged capital, for example "Et", "Iocundum" and "Qui".
- A large red "C" initial sits in the right page, column d, about two-thirds of the way down (img-015, img-020).
- Small red marginal sigla stand in the outer and inner margins against particular lines: "ag" (or "a" with a "g"-like tail), sometimes with two dots above, plus "c" with two dots above, and "ca". Their meaning is not determined.
- In the upper part of the right page, column d, large black display letters "Po D..co.." (img-005; overview "PoDiscor"?) are written over the text in a later, darker ink. They appear to be a later addition.
- The left page: column a is narrow and broken by a crease. Its outer part shows as a separate strip (img-002, img-007, img-012, img-017), but near the bottom the strip and the inner part fall on the same text lines (see below). Column b is the full column. The top margin is folded over (img-004 to img-006), and the fold carries a few lines of text above the red top ruling.
- Damage: water staining, especially left page column b and right page column d; holes; folds; abrasion in the lower half of column d (img-015, img-016).

SELECTED SPANS: column b of the left page (whole visible column), column c of the right page (whole), column d of the right page (top half well read, lower half partial), and readable parts of column a. Unread or largely unread: the lower half of column d (abraded, img-016, img-020, img-021) and the outer strip of column a (only line-ends).
